claims.text: A thin, high-temperature-stable self-lubricating coating can be applied to CoCrFeNi.
The coating will promote in situ formation of a lubricious tribofilm during sliding.
The coating and resulting tribofilm will lower friction from room temperature to 800 °C.
The coating and resulting tribofilm will lower wear from room temperature to 800 °C.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi exhibits elevated friction and wear at temperature extremes.
Physical vapor deposition is a suitable method for depositing the proposed coating uniformly on CoCrFeNi.
Under sliding at elevated temperature, the coating will develop or maintain a continuous, adherent, lubricious oxide or tribofilm at the contact interface.
The coating will oxidize in a controlled manner during sliding to form the lubricious film.
The lubricious film will reduce direct asperity contact.
Reducing direct asperity contact will reduce friction and wear.
The coating's high-temperature stability will preserve its lubricating behavior as temperature and load vary.
Coated CoCrFeNi will have a lower and more consistent coefficient of friction than uncoated CoCrFeNi across approximately 25–800 °C.
Coated CoCrFeNi will have a lower wear rate than uncoated CoCrFeNi across approximately 25–800 °C.
The coating will provide improved tribological performance near 704 °C and at the temperature extremes.
The coating's benefits are expected in oxygen-rich environments.
The coating may be ineffective or less effective in inert atmospheres.
The coating may be ineffective or less effective under loads far above the tested range.
